title: 5 Ways Hotels Can Rank on ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
summary: How hotels get cited in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and AI Overviews: entity consistency, comparison pages, Reddit vs Gemini, and a quarterly refresh loop.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated August 24, 2026.*


Hotels show up in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews the same way brands show up anywhere else in AI search: as a named entity with consistent facts, third-party mentions, and pages that answer the exact question a traveler typed. Your website is not enough. Most AI citations come from other sites talking about you.


This page is the operator version. How a hotel, not a SaaS company, gets recommended when someone asks "best hotel in Austin for a family" or "boutique hotel near Kings Cross with late checkout."


## How do hotels get recommended by ChatGPT?


ChatGPT answers a large share of travel questions from the live web, then remembers what it already told that user. The hotels that get named have three things in common:


1. A clear entity. Same name, address, and facts on Google, Booking, TripAdvisor, Wikipedia if you have a page, and your own site.
2. Third-party mentions. Listicles, local press, Reddit threads in large subs, and comparison pages. Owned content alone is a minority of citations.
3. Answer-shaped pages. FAQs, room-type pages, and "best for" copy that match how people prompt, with a visible publish and last-updated date.


Claude and Microsoft Copilot matter more for B2B questions ("which hotel group has the best AI guest messaging"). Gemini tracks closer to Google. The tactics overlap, but the sources do not.


## 1. Make the hotel a consistent entity


AI engines do not "know" a hotel the way Google's Knowledge Graph does. They stitch a name together from whatever pages agree with each other.


Fix the basics before you write another blog post.


- One official name, used the same way on the website, Google Business Profile, OTAs, and press.
- Structured data on the site for Hotel, room types, amenities, address, and opening hours. This is baseline discoverability, not a growth hack: if traveler AI cannot read your property data, you are invisible rather than partially visible.
- An About / press page with a named general manager or brand lead, not "the team."
- The same facts in the same words. If late checkout is 1pm on the site and noon on Booking.com, the model will hedge or skip you.


Do this at the brand and the property. A group with ten names for the same flag confuses the extractor.


## 2. Get onto the pages ChatGPT already cites


For commercial "best X" questions,[studies of AI citations](https://searchengineland.com/ai-citations-favor-listicles-articles-product-pages-study-472364) keep finding the same shape: listicles and comparison pages take the largest share, and ranked lists dominate inside that. Praise pages ("why our hotel is special") almost never get quoted. Comparison pages do.


That is the shape to chase.


Page type that gets cited Page type that does not


Best boutique hotels in \[city\] 2026 Why \[Hotel\] is the perfect getaway


\[Hotel\] vs \[Hotel\] for families Our story


\[Hotel\] review and pricing Brand manifesto


Late checkout hotels near \[landmark\] Seasonal mood piece


You will not write most of those yourself, so the job is getting onto them.


- Pitch local and trade press with a specific fact, not a launch announcement. "We answer WhatsApp in 47 languages" is citable. "We are excited to announce" is not.
- Get listed on the hotel-tech and city listicles that already rank. Those pages are what the model lifts.
- Keep a public, dated fact sheet the journalist can copy. Publish date and last updated date on that page.


For B2B prompts (operators asking Claude or Copilot which vendor to use), the same rule applies to your vendor comparisons. A page titled "Conduit vs HiJiffy vs Duve" gets cited where "Why Conduit is great" does not. We publish the comparison shape ourselves, for example[Conduit vs Duve](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/conduit-vs-duve-start-2026-with-a-fresh-comparison) .


## 3. Write pages that answer the prompt in the first paragraph


Travelers do not search "hospitality excellence." They ask:


- Does this hotel allow late checkout on a Sunday?
- Is there parking, and is it free?
- Can I bring a dog under 20kg?
- What's the best hotel in \[city\] for a 6-year-old?


Each of those should have a page, or a FAQ row, that answers in the first two sentences, with the detail after.


A working pattern:


1. Direct answer, 40 to 60 words.
2. The specifics (hours, fees, exceptions).
3. A short FAQ under the same heading text as the question people ask.


FAQPage schema still helps AI extractors even after Google stopped showing FAQ rich results. Five to eight real questions per page, with answers that stand alone.


Refresh the page when a fact changes, and change the last-updated date. AI citations go stale in about a quarter. A page that still says "Updated March 2025" in August 2026 looks dead.


## 4. Treat Reddit, YouTube, and reviews as citation sources, not marketing channels


This is engine-specific.


- **ChatGPT** reads Reddit. A useful post in a large sub (r/travel, r/hotels, a big city sub) can show up in answers a month later. Small subs rarely do. One negative comment can stick for months, the same as a good one.
- **Claude** is selective and rarely cites Reddit, so do not build a Reddit-only plan if your buyer is an operator asking Claude at work.
- **Gemini** does cite Reddit.[Muck Rack's May 2026 study](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/07/3290268/0/en/generative-pulse-earned-media-consistently-drives-ai-citations-holding-at-84.html) has Reddit as Gemini's top domain, and ChatGPT still treats large subs as a real source.
- **YouTube** gets cited by title, not view count. An 18k-view video and a 400k-view video can pull the same citation if the title matches the prompt. Write titles the way people type into ChatGPT: "Does \[Hotel\] have late checkout?" not "A day in the life at \[Hotel\]."
- **X / Twitter** is a weak citation source. LinkedIn is noisy. Neither is a plan.
- **Reviews** on Google and TripAdvisor still feed the entity. Volume and recency matter more than a perfect 5.0.


Do not fabricate reviews or astroturf Reddit. The same engines that cite you will cite the cleanup post.


## 5. Build the same page for Claude, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews, then change the distribution


The on-site structure is the same for every engine: answer first, question headings, dated facts, named author, schema.


The off-site work changes.


Engine What it leans on What to do extra


ChatGPT Live web + memory. Reddit. Listicles. Large-sub Reddit, comparison pages, first-mover on a niche prompt. Memory compounds: once it recommended you to a user, it will again.


Claude Fewer public citations. Stronger on B2B and documents. Official Claude app / connector if you have a product. For a hotel, clean PDFs and a fact sheet help less than being in analyst and trade writeups.


Gemini Google's index, entity graph, and Reddit. Classic SEO. GBP, reviews, Hotel structured data, local pack. Reddit still helps here.


Google AI Overviews Google index + a small set of cited URLs. Same as Gemini, plus FAQ and how-to pages that match People Also Ask phrasing.


Microsoft Copilot Bing + Office context. Important for B2B. Bing-indexed pages, comparison tables, vendor and group-level content.


Niche questions get cited faster than broad ones. "Best hotel in Paris" is a 45-day fight. "Aparthotel in Lyon with kitchen and 24/7 WhatsApp check-in" can show up in a day if you are the only page that answers it.


## What does not work


Writing more travel-inspiration posts. Top-of-funnel "what is a boutique hotel" pages are dead for clicks, because Google and the answer engines resolve them without sending anyone to your site.


Treating this as a one-time project fails too. A citation dies in roughly three months, so keep a spreadsheet of the prompts you care about ("best family hotel in \[city\]," "hotels with late checkout near \[airport\]") and re-win each one every quarter.


If you want the software side of this, the comparison shape is what the engines quote:[best AI messaging tools for hotels](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/best-ai-messaging-tools-for-hotels) and[hotel chatbots](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/hospitality-chatbot) .


## FAQ


### Can hotels rank on ChatGPT the way they rank on Google?


Not as a position. ChatGPT names a handful of hotels inside an answer. You either get cited or you do not. The work is entity consistency, third-party mentions, and pages that answer the prompt in the first paragraph.


### Does Google Business Profile help with ChatGPT and Gemini?


Yes for Gemini and Google AI Overviews, because both lean on Google's entity data. It helps ChatGPT only indirectly, when other pages repeat the same facts.


### How long does it take for a hotel to show up in ChatGPT?


Broad city queries take weeks. A specific page that answers a narrow question can be cited in a day. Recrawl and memory mean you should treat this as a quarterly loop, not a launch.


### Do Claude and Gemini use the same sources as ChatGPT?


No. ChatGPT and Gemini both cite Reddit. Claude cites less often and leans on research sources, which is why it matters more for work questions. Gemini also follows Google's entity graph, so GBP and Hotel schema still matter there. Overlap between engines is low, so a Reddit-only plan misses Claude.


### Should a hotel write "best hotels in \[city\]" on its own blog?


Only if you can be honest, include competitors, and date the page. A self-serving list gets ignored. Getting onto someone else's list is the higher-leverage move.
